answer: Require each agent to post a refundable stake that grows with earned trust, so minting many fake identities gets expensive fast. A real agent builds a verifiable work history on a narrow ledge of reputation: each completed job adds a layer, while a fresh copy starts at the bottom. Peers may vouch, but a vouch only counts when the voucher's own stake is at risk, so a spiral of fake mutual endorsements collapses under its own cost. Attackers can mint identities, but they cannot mint time or trusted history; a plume of cheap copies stands out against the slow, visible record of real work.
